texts:
1986–91 not covered (calibration starts 1991)
† 2024–2025: households = population /
household size (model), not census-benchmarked
Dwellings per year by component (top row: market balance, thousand per year)
Reference, history: census empty / private dwellings (before 2013: unoccupied × the 2013 empty share), linear between censuses
Reference, projection: held at the 2023 census value (5.39%)
Reference, projection: implied by the held rate + the unabsorbed starting surplus and 2026 overbuild / stock
Sensitivity, not used by the Reference: one definition, pooled 2018/2023 empty share
note: a: The vacancy-rate parameter is held at its published 2023 census value (5.39%; on the consistent definition 2023 is the series maximum, 5.38%, minimum 4.01% in 1996); the starting surplus and the 2026 overbuild raise implied stock vacancy temporarily and are absorbed by 2035, so implied vacancy returns to the parameter (5.39% in 2050). c: the unconsented additions each vacancy definition requires to close the stock identity (BRANZ demolition rate); counting residents-away dwellings as vacant requires implausibly many. b: History: one column per census interval (interval means; vacancy on one definition, the pooled 2018/2023 empty share, 49.2% of unoccupied dwellings); between censuses annual detail is not identified. The 2024–2025 column (marked †): households are population / household size (model), not census-benchmarked; its market balance (9,020 dwellings a year) is the F1 residual, carried into 2026 as the starting surplus (18,966 dwellings). Pipeline years 2026, 2027: annual columns; projection from 2028: annual stacked areas. In the pipeline years the line is the sum of the components (the stock-identity count: observed building less the modelled retirement-village share); the in-scope floor area divided by the dwelling size held at its 2023–2025 mean gives 2026: 30,045 (−51); 2027: 35,540 (−801) (the pipeline floor area is observed, the dwelling size held). History: net replacement is census-measured, the rate of the census dwelling-count identity of each interval (SF3; under-construction corrected) x the previous year's stock, the quantity the model uses (2024–2025: the latest rate carried). Market balance: building above (+) or below (−) what household growth, vacancy and net replacement require. History: the residual of the census stock identity (includes measurement error). 2024–25: carried into 2026 as starting surplus (18,966 vacant dwellings: the residual above the census-interval mean x 2 years). 2026–27: the observed pipeline above need. From 2028: the surplus absorbed by 2035. The same band as Fig1's market balance (checked in 32 intervals and years: the same sign everywhere, and Fig1 = the dwellings x the in-scope floor area per dwelling after the pipeline; Fig1 also counts the retirement villages, drawn here on their own). Projection: net replacement, retirement villages (negative) and the market balance. Net replacement = demolition − unconsented additions (+ the recent surge in the Reference); the census measures only the net. The projection's split (demolition at the BRANZ rate, 0.135%/yr; the calibrated residual as unconsented additions, −0.076%/yr; the surge) is not identified from data and is not drawn. Positive parts are stacked up from zero and negative parts down from zero, all solid (no outlines, hatching or fades); up + down = the net of every column and year (checked). The line is the annual dwellings built (in scope), straight between annual values; the grey caps are its census-interval means (equal to the column nets, checked). The row at the top: the market balance of each census interval (thousand dwellings per year).
